brief: Goldman Sachs equity sales daily roundup. The S&P rose 106bps to 7748, up 13% year to date, led by Mag7 at +2.5% with all seven higher. Dovish Waller comments helped: he said recent data show some signs of disinflation and that if that continues over the next two weeks he would be inclined to support holding the funds rate. Market-implied odds of a September Fed hike fell to 52% from 66% on Wednesday and the 10-year fell to 4.76%. Against that, 54% of the PCE basket has risen more than 3% over 12 months, the highest in three years. Goldman estimates today's payrolls at +40k versus +55k consensus because big-data job indicators slowed and August initial prints carry a consistent negative bias. A cited colleague argues token prices are collapsing faster than consumption can grow, so more AI demand at lower prices is not automatically bullish, compute oversupply becomes plausible, and that helps explain the space de-rating. Goldman prefers equity to credit on tight spreads, late-cycle re-leveraging and AI-related debt issuance. Europe at 14.5x P/E and a 5.3% FCF yield is not overpriced.
